tales.credit: Public-domain Little Red Riding Hood tradition

text.en: Once, a gentle girl in a bright red hood set out through the whispering woods to visit her grandmother, carrying a basket of warm bread and sweet butter. Sunlight flickered between the leaves, and birds sang soft warnings she was too kind to hear. A cunning wolf stepped from the shadows and asked, in a honey voice, where she was going. "To Grandmother's cottage," she answered, holding the basket close. The wolf ran ahead along a darker path, swallowed the grandmother whole, and slipped into her nightcap and bed. When the girl arrived, she felt a chill — "Grandmother, what big eyes you have… what big teeth!" The wolf sprang; she cried out in terror. A woodcutter heard that cry, burst through the door, and drove the wolf into the forest. Grandmother and child held each other, hearts still pounding, and the little red hood never again walked that lonely path alone.
text.yue: 從前有個溫柔女仔戴住鮮紅帽，拎住熱麵包同甜牛油籃，穿過沙沙作響嘅樹林去探婆婆。陽光喺葉隙間閃，雀仔輕輕唱警告，但佢太善良聽唔入耳。一隻狡猾嘅狼由陰影走出嚟，用蜜糖聲問佢去邊。「去婆婆屋企呀。」佢將籃抱實答。狼行暗路搶先，吞咗婆婆，戴起睡帽瞓上床。女仔入到屋覺得凍：「婆婆，你隻眼好大……你啲牙好大！」狼撲出嚟，佢嚇到大叫。樵夫聽到衝入屋，將狼趕入森林。婆婆同女仔攬住對方，心跳未定；之後小紅帽再唔會一個人行嗰條寂寞小路。
text.zh: 从前有个温柔的女孩戴着鲜红帽子，提着热面包和甜黄油篮子，穿过沙沙作响的树林去看望外婆。阳光在叶隙间闪烁，鸟儿轻轻唱着警告，可她太善良听不进去。一只狡猾的狼从阴影里走出来，用蜜糖般的声音问她去哪里。“去外婆家。”她抱紧篮子回答。狼走暗路抢先，吞下外婆，戴上睡帽躺上床。女孩进门感到一阵寒意：“外婆，你的眼睛好大……你的牙好大！”狼扑过来，她吓得大叫。樵夫听见冲进屋，把狼赶进森林。外婆和孩子紧紧相拥，心还在跳；从此小红帽再也不独自走那条寂寞小路。
text.ja: むかし、あたたかいパンと甘いバターの籠を抱えた赤い頭巾のやさしい少女が、木々のささやく森を抜けておばあさんを訪ねました。木漏れ日が揺れ、鳥がそっと警告を歌いましたが、彼女は優しすぎて聞き逃しました。ずる賢い狼が影から現れ、蜜のような声で行き先を尋ねます。「おばあさんのお家へ」と彼女は籠を抱きしめて答えました。狼は暗い道を先回りし、おばあさんを飲みこみ、ナイトキャップをかぶってベッドに横になりました。少女は寒気を感じ、「おばあさん、なんて大きな目……なんて大きな歯」と言うと狼が飛びかかり、彼女は恐れて叫びました。木こりがその声を聞き、戸を破って狼を森へ追い払い、二人は胸を寄せ合って安心しました。それから少女は、二度とその寂しい道を一人では歩きませんでした。

text.en: Three little pigs left home with hopeful hearts, each dreaming of a safe place of their own. The first built quickly of straw, laughing as the wind played through the walls. The second chose sticks, humming while he worked. The third pig, quieter and careful, laid brick upon brick until his house stood warm and strong. Then a hungry wolf came breathing hard. "Little pig, little pig, let me come in!" he howled. "Not by the hair of my chinny chin chin!" cried each brother. The wolf huffed and puffed the straw house down, then the stick house, and the two frightened pigs raced to the brick cottage, trembling in each other's arms. At the brick door the wolf blew until he was dizzy — the walls did not move. He tried the chimney, tumbled into a pot of hot water, and fled howling into the night.
text.yue: 三隻小豬懷住希望離開屋企，各自想有個安全嘅家。大哥用禾稈起得好快，笑住任風穿牆。二哥用樹枝，一面做一面哼歌。細佬安靜又小心，一塊磚一塊磚起，屋企又暖又穩。之後一隻肚餓嘅狼喘住氣嚟：「小豬小豬，俾我入嚟！」每隻都喊：「唔得！」狼吹冧禾稈屋同樹枝屋，兩隻嚇到震嘅豬仔跑入磚屋，攬住對方發抖。喺磚門前狼吹到頭暈——牆唔郁。佢由煙囪爬入，跌落熱水煲，嚎住逃入夜。三隻小豬喺火旁分麵包，感激耐心、勇氣，同一個撐得住嘅家。
text.zh: 三只小猪怀着希望离开家，各自梦想有个安全的窝。大哥用稻草盖得很快，笑着任风穿墙。二哥用树枝，一边做一边哼歌。小弟安静又仔细，一块砖一块砖砌，房子又暖又稳。后来一只饿狼喘着气来了：“小猪小猪，让我进去！”每只都喊：“不行！”狼吹倒了稻草屋和树枝屋，两只吓得发抖的小猪跑进砖房，互相紧紧抱着。在砖门前狼吹到头晕——墙纹丝不动。他从烟囱爬进去，掉进热水锅，嚎叫着逃进夜色。三只小猪在火旁分面包，感激耐心、勇气和一个撑得住的家。
text.ja: 三匹の子ぶたは希望を胸に家を出て、それぞれ安全な居場所を夢見ました。長男はわらで大急ぎの家を建て、風が壁をぬけるのを笑いました。次男は木の枝で、口ずさみながら作りました。末の子は静かで慎重に、レンガを重ねてあたたかく強い家を建てました。やがて腹をすかせた狼が息を荒げて来ます。「子ぶたよ、入れておくれ！」と吠え、「絶対にだめ！」と兄弟は答えました。狼はわらの家と枝の家を吹き倒し、震える二匹はレンガの家へ逃げ込み、抱き合いました。レンガの戸口で狼はめまいがするほど吹きましたが壁は動きません。煙突から入り熱い鍋に落ち、夜へ逃げ去りました。三匹は火のそばでパンを分け、忍耐と勇気、そして守ってくれる家に感謝しました。

text.en: In a busy farmyard one late summer, a last egg cracked open and a hatchling stepped out who looked nothing like the other ducklings. His feathers were grey, his neck too long, and the farmyard laughed. "What an ugly thing," said the old duck, and the little ones pecked him away from the bread crumbs. Night after night he hid behind the reeds, whispering to the moon, "Where do I belong?" Autumn painted the pond gold; winter locked it in ice. He wandered alone through frost and hunger, almost forgetting the sound of kindness. When spring returned, the ice sang as it broke, and he saw three graceful swans gliding on open water. Shame bowed his head — then he saw his own reflection: white feathers, a long proud neck, a swan among swans. The others drifted near and touched him with soft wings. "You were never ugly," the wind seemed to say. "You were only becoming." Tears of relief warmed his bill, and he finally understood that patience and gentle hope can outlast every cruel word.
text.yue: 農場入面有隻遲出世嘅小鴨同其他鴨仔唔一樣，成日被人笑。佢走過秋天同嚴冬，又凍又孤單，一路想有個歸屬。春天返嚟，佢見到湖面優雅嘅天鵝就低頭——然後睇到自己倒影：原來自己都變成天鵝。其他天鵝歡迎佢，用軟翼輕輕掂住。風好似講：「你從來唔醜，你只係未長成。」解脫嘅淚暖住喙，佢明白耐心同善良，勝過刻薄說話。
text.zh: 农场里有只晚出生的小鸭和其他鸭子不一样，总被取笑。他走过秋天和严冬，又冷又孤单，一直想找到归属。春天来了，他看见水面上优雅的天鹅，低下头——却看见自己的倒影：原来自己也长成了天鹅。其他天鹅欢迎他，用柔软的翅膀轻轻碰他。风仿佛说：“你从不丑陋，你只是还在长成。”解脱的泪水温暖了喙，他明白耐心与善良胜过刻薄的话。
text.ja: 農場で遅く生まれたひなはほかのアヒルと違って見え、からかわれました。秋と厳しい冬をさまよい、寒さと孤独の中で居場所を探し続けました。春になると湖の白鳥を見てうつむき、水面に映る自分が白鳥になっているのに気づきました。仲間に迎えられ柔らかい翼で触れられ、忍耐とやさしさが意地悪な言葉に勝つと知りました。

text.en: By the cold hearth, Cinderella scrubbed ash from her hands while her stepsisters laughed into mirrors, dressing for the royal ball. "You stay home," they said, and her heart ached with quiet longing. Then a soft light filled the kitchen — a fairy godmother with kind eyes. "You shall go," she whispered, turning a pumpkin into a gleaming coach, mice into proud horses, and rags into a gown that shimmered like moonlight. "Be home by midnight, my dear — the magic ends then." At the palace the prince could not look away; they danced as if the world had slowed just for them. When the clock struck twelve she fled down the steps, leaving one glass slipper flashing on the stone. The prince searched every house; the slipper fit only Cinderella's gentle foot. She forgave her family with trembling courage, and the hall filled not with triumph alone but with a kinder joy — the joy of being seen at last for who she truly was.
text.yue: 灰姑娘喺凍爐邊做嘢，繼姊對住鏡笑住準備舞會。仙女教母將南瓜變馬車、老鼠變馬、破衫變禮服，叮囑午夜魔法會完。王子成晚同佢跳舞，十二點鐘響佢匆忙走，留低一隻玻璃鞋。王子四處試鞋，得灰姑娘啱。佢用顫抖勇氣原諒家人，王宮多咗份溫柔快樂——終於被人睇見真正自己。
text.zh: 灰姑娘在冰冷炉边干活，姐姐们对着镜子笑着准备舞会。仙女教母把南瓜变成马车、老鼠变成马、破衣变成礼服，并提醒午夜魔法会消失。王子整晚与她共舞，十二点钟响她匆忙离开，留下一只水晶鞋。王子走遍全国试鞋，只有灰姑娘合适。她以颤抖的勇气原谅家人，王宫里多了更温柔的快乐——终于被看见真实的自己。
text.ja: シンデレラは冷たい炉端で働き、姉たちは鏡に笑いながら舞踏会の支度をしました。妖精の助けでカボチャは馬車に、ネズミは馬に、ぼろはドレスになり、真夜中に魔法が解けると告げられました。王子と踊り明かした彼女は十二時に逃げ、ガラスの靴を残しました。靴が合うのはシンデレラだけで、彼女は震える勇気で家族を許し、ほんとうの自分を見てもらえたあたたかい喜びに包まれました。

title.ja: ヘンゼルとグレーテル

text.en: In a lean year when the cupboards whispered emptiness, Hansel and Gretel were led deep into a forest that smelled of pine and fear. Hansel squeezed his sister's hand. "Do not be afraid," he said, and dropped pale pebbles that shone like tiny moons along the dark path. By moonlight they followed the trail home, and for one night their father's arms felt safe again; their stepmother's silence still chilled the room. The next journey left them with only breadcrumbs; birds ate every crumb, and the path vanished into green shadow. Lost and hungry, Gretel cried softly while Hansel kept walking. At last they found a cottage of bread walls and sugar windows that glittered like hope against the gloom. A thin voice invited them in with sweets — then the door locked with a click that stole their breath. The witch's eyes were cold as iron. She caged Hansel to fatten him and set Gretel to hard work by the fire. Night after night Gretel whispered through the bars, "I will not leave you — hold on." When the witch ordered her to check the oven heat, clever Gretel asked for a lesson; as the witch leaned in, Gretel pushed with all her love and fear, and the cruel spell ended in fire and smoke. Freeing her brother with shaking hands, they filled their pockets with pearls from the cottage chests, hearts still racing. A shining bird led them to a wide lake; a kind duck carried them across cool water under a pale sky. They returned to their father with treasure, warm bread, and tears that tasted of home — proof that courage shared between two small hearts can outshine the darkest wood.
text.yue: 饑荒時候，韓賽爾同葛雷特被人帶入深林。韓賽爾第一次掉白石仔，月光帶佢哋返屋企。第二次得丟麵包屑，雀仔食晒。迷路又攰，佢哋見到麵包同糖砌嘅屋。巫婆用甜食歡迎，之後鎖起韓賽爾想養肥做晚餐。聰明嘅葛雷特將巫婆推入爐，救出哥哥，由屋入面嘅箱袋滿珍珠。跟住隻發光雀仔去到大湖，一隻善良嘅鴨載佢哋過水。返到爸爸身邊，有珍寶、暖包，同返屋企嘅安心——兩顆細小心臟分享嘅勇氣，照亮最黑樹林。
text.zh: 饥荒时，韩赛尔和格雷特被带进深林。韩赛尔第一次扔下白石子，月光引他们回家。第二次只能丢面包屑，被鸟吃光了。又累又迷路时，他们发现一间面包和糖做成的小屋。女巫先用甜食欢迎，再把韩赛尔关进笼子准备养肥当晚餐。聪明的格雷特把女巫推进炉子，救出哥哥，从屋里的箱子装满珍珠。跟着一只发光的鸟来到大湖，一只善良的鸭子载他们过水。他们回到父亲身边，带着珍宝、热面包和回家的安心——两颗小小心脏分享的勇气，能照亮最黑的树林。
text.ja: 飢饉のころ、ヘンゼルとグレーテルは森の奥へ連れて行かれました。ヘンゼルは白い小石を落とし、月明かりで一度は家に戻れました。次はパンくずしか追えず、鳥に食べられてしまいました。迷って疲れた兄妹はパンと砂糖の小屋を見つけます。魔女はお菓子でもてなし、ヘンゼルをかごに閉じ込めて太らせようとしました。賢いグレーテルは魔女を炉に押し込み、兄を助け、小屋の箱から真珠を鞄に詰めました。光る鳥に導かれて広い湖へ行き、やさしい鴨に乗って渡り、宝物と温かいパン、そして家の安堵を抱えて父のもとへ戻りました。

text.en: A king and queen invited every fairy but one to bless their newborn daughter. Music filled the hall; gifts of beauty, grace, and song were laid upon the cradle like soft light. Then the uninvited fairy swept in on a cold wind that made the candles shiver. "She shall prick her finger on a spindle and die," she hissed, and fear froze every heart in the room. A kinder fairy stepped forward, eyes shining with mercy. "Not death," she said softly, laying a hand above the child, "but a sleep as deep as winter — until love finds her and wakes her gently." Years passed in careful joy; spindles were banned, yet curiosity still grew. On her fifteenth birthday the princess wandered the quiet towers alone and found an old woman spinning gold thread. "What is that bright wheel?" she asked, curious as morning. The spindle kissed her finger; she fell as if into a dream, and the whole castle slept with her — cooks mid-stir, dogs mid-bark, roses climbing the walls, silence thick as velvet. A hundred years later a brave prince heard the old tale and cut through thorns that had grown into a living wall, scratching his hands yet never turning back. He found her still as snow, and his gentle kiss was not conquest but tenderness and hope. She woke with a breath like spring; the court woke to music and morning light pouring through dusty windows. They married in the great hall, and the kingdom remembered that mercy can rewrite a cruel spell into a second chance — and that true waking begins with kindness.
text.yue: 國王王后請仙女祝福初生公主，但有個冇獲邀嘅仙女咒佢會被紡錘刺傷而死。另一個善良仙女將死亡改成長睡。十五歲生日，公主喺高塔掂到紡錘就瞓着，成座城堡喺玫瑰同靜默底下一齊瞓。一百年後勇敢王子斬開長成牆嘅荊棘，輕輕一吻叫醒佢，宮廷隨音樂同晨光醒來。佢哋喺大廳結婚，王國記得仁慈可以將惡咒改寫成第二次機會——真正醒來由善良開始。
text.zh: 国王王后请仙女祝福新生公主，却有个未被邀请的仙女诅咒她会被纺锤刺伤而死。另一位善良仙女把死亡改成长睡。十五岁生日那天，公主在高塔碰到纺锤沉睡，整座城堡在玫瑰与寂静中一起睡着。一百年后勇敢的王子拨开长成墙的荆棘，轻轻一吻唤醒她，宫廷随音乐和晨光醒来。他们在大厅结婚，王国记得仁慈可以把恶咒改写成第二次机会——真正的醒来从善良开始。
text.ja: 王と王妃は生まれた姫に妖精の祝福を願いましたが、招かれなかった妖精は紡錘で指を刺して死ぬ呪いをかけました。やさしい妖精は死を長い眠りに変えました。十五の誕生日、姫は塔で紡錘に触れ、城中がバラと静寂の中で共に眠りました。百年後、勇敢な王子が壁のように伸びた茨を切り開き、やさしい口づけで姫を起こすと、音楽と朝の光の中で宮廷が目覚めました。大広間で結ばれ、情けが残酷な呪いを二度目のチャンスへ書き換えると国は覚えました。

text.en: A queen once stood by a window in winter, wishing aloud for a child as white as snow, as red as blood, and as black as ebony wood. Soon Snow-White was born with a laugh like a bell, and the queen's joy was soft and fierce. After she died, a vain stepmother asked her magic mirror who was fairest in the land. Day after day the mirror answered her name — until one morning it named Snow-White, and envy grew sharp as broken glass in the queen's chest. "Take her into the forest," she ordered a huntsman, "and do not bring her home." The huntsman raised his knife beneath the pines, then lowered it, trembling with shame. "Run, child," he whispered, tears in his beard, and she fled through roots and shadows until her legs ached and she found a cottage of seven dwarfs. They returned at dusk, surprised, then kind. "You may stay," they said, warming soup, "if you keep house with care and share our evening bread." For a time the cottage glowed with laughter, shared songs, and the comfort of belonging. Three times the stepmother came in disguise — first with a lace pulled too tight around Snow-White's breath, then a poisoned comb that burned her scalp, and at last a red apple that smelled of summer orchards. "One bite, sweet girl," she coaxed with a smile that did not reach her eyes. Snow-White fell as if dead among the flowers. The dwarfs wept through the night and laid her in a glass coffin on the mountain so the birds could still see her peaceful face. A prince riding by begged to take the coffin home with honor; when his servants stumbled on a root, the apple piece slipped from her lips and she drew a clean breath of cold mountain air. She woke to tears, cheers, and soft dwarfs' hands. They married with the dwarfs as guests of honor, and the cruel queen faced the truth her mirror could no longer hide — that beauty without mercy is only a shadow, while kindness endures and lights the darkest glass.
text.yue: 皇后願望有個似雪咁白、似血咁紅、似烏木咁黑嘅孩子，於是白雪公主出世。皇后去世後，愛美嘅後母問魔鏡邊個最靚；鏡講係白雪，嫉妒就似玻璃咁尖。獵人奉命將女仔丟喺森林，但佢放生咗佢，白雪搵到七個小矮人嘅小屋，答應用心打理同分享晚餐麵包就可以留低。後母三次喬裝嚟：緊身帶、毒梳，最後係好似夏天咁甜嘅毒蘋果。白雪好似死咗，小矮人將佢放喺山上玻璃棺。王子請求帶棺返去；僕人喺樹根絆跌，蘋果塊由嘴跌出，佢吸入清新空氣醒返。婚禮請小矮人做貴賓，惡毒皇后要面對鏡再也隱唔住嘅真相——冇仁慈嘅美只係影，善良先至長久。
text.zh: 王后祈愿有个像雪一样白、像血一样红、像乌木一样黑的孩子，于是白雪公主出生了。王后去世后，爱美的继母问魔镜谁最美；镜子说出白雪时，嫉妒变得像玻璃一样锋利。猎人奉命把女孩丢在森林，却放了她一马；白雪找到七个小矮人的小屋，答应用心持家并分享晚餐面包便可留下。继母三次乔装而来：束带、毒梳，最后是看起来像夏日一样甜的毒苹果。白雪像死去一样，小矮人把她放进山上的玻璃棺。王子请求把棺柩带回家；仆人被树根绊倒时，苹果块从嘴里掉出，她吸入清新空气醒来。婚礼请小矮人做贵宾，恶毒的王后面对镜子再也藏不住的真相——没有仁慈的美只是影子，善良才会长久。
text.ja: 王妃は雪のように白く、血のように赤く、黒檀のように黒い子を願って白雪姫が生まれました。王妃の死後、高慢な継母は鏡に誰が一番美しいか問い、鏡が白雪姫と答えると嫉妬はガラスのように鋭くなりました。狩人が森に捨てるよう命じられましたが彼女を助け、七人の小人の小屋に着き、家事をきちんとして夜のパンを分かち合えば滞在できると言われました。継母は三度変装し、締めつける紐、毒のくし、そして夏のように甘く見える毒りんごを届けました。白雪姫は死んだように倒れ、小人たちは山のガラスの棺に安置しました。王子が棺を家へ運ぶと、従者が根につまずいてりんごの欠片が口から落ち、姫は澄んだ空気を吸って目覚めました。小人を賓客に迎えて結ばれ、残酷な王妃は鏡が隠せなくなった真実に向き合うことになりました。

text.en: Deep under the sea, where light filtered green and soft through kelp forests, the youngest mermaid princess listened for the world above — ships creaking, church bells, and human laughter she had never touched with her hands. Her sisters brought back stories; she brought back longing. On her fifteenth year she rose through the foam under a wild sky, and a storm tore a prince from his ship into black water. She held his head above the waves, her heart pounding with a love so sudden it hurt her chest, and left him breathing on the shore though he never saw her true face among the spray. Night after night in her coral bed she dreamed of his eyes and the warmth of air. She swam to a sea witch in a cave that smelled of salt and fear. The bargain was cruel: her bright singing voice for human legs, and every step would feel like knives on marble. "Still," she signed with trembling hands, "I will try — for love." Mute and graceful she danced for the prince in palace gardens under lantern light; he cared for her as a dear friend, stroking her hair, yet chose another bride whose smile felt familiar from a rescue he could not quite remember. On the wedding night her sisters rose from the deep with a knife bright as fish-scale. "End him," they pleaded through tears, "and come home to foam and family — we miss your song." Tears burned her silent throat. She looked at the sleeping prince, kissed him once with all the words she could not speak, threw the knife into the dark waves, and stepped herself into the pale dawn beyond the ship. Instead of vanishing she became a bright daughter of the air, earning a soul by choosing mercy over revenge. The sea kept her song in its shells, and every morning remembered her courage — that the bravest love sometimes means letting go, and still becoming more than you were.
text.yue: 海底最細嗰個美人魚公主好嚮往浪上面有船同教堂鐘聲嘅世界。十五歲浮出海面，喺風暴中救咗遇難王子，遠遠咁愛佢，但王子喺泡沫入面睇唔到真正嘅佢。佢同海巫交易：用清亮嘅聲換人腳，每一步好似大理石上嘅利刀。佢啞住喺王宮花園優美跳舞；王子當佢係親愛朋友，最後娶咗另一個帶熟悉笑容嘅新娘。婚禮夜，姊姊由深海帶刀上嚟——如果結束王子就可以返泡沫同家人——但佢將刀掟落黑浪，自己躍入淡淡黎明。冇消失，反而變成空氣嘅明亮女兒，用仁慈勝過報復換靈魂。海喺貝殼入面留低佢首歌，每個清晨都記得佢嘅勇氣。
text.zh: 海底最小的美人鱼公主向往浪上有船和教堂钟声的世界。十五岁那年她浮出海面，在风暴中救了遇难的王子，远远地爱着他，王子却在泡沫里看不见真正的她。她与海巫交易：用清亮的声音换成人腿，每一步都像大理石上的利刃。她哑着在王宫花园里优雅起舞；王子把她当亲爱的朋友，却另娶了一个带着熟悉笑容的新娘。婚礼夜，姐姐们从深海带刀上来——若结束王子便可回到泡沫与家人——可她把刀扔进黑浪，自己跃入淡淡黎明。她没有消失，而成了空气中明亮的女儿，用仁慈胜过报复赢得灵魂。海在贝壳里留下她的歌，每个清晨都记得她的勇气。
text.ja: 海の底で末の人魚姫は、船と教会の鐘がある波の上の世界に憧れていました。十五歳で海面に上がり嵐の難破から王子を助け、遠くから愛しましたが、王子は泡の中で本当の姿を知りません。彼女は海の魔女と取引し、澄んだ声と引き換えに人の足を得て、歩むたび大理石の上の刃物のような痛みを覚えました。声を失ったまま宮殿の庭で優雅に踊り、王子は大切な友として接しましたが、見慣れた笑顔の別の花嫁を選びました。婚礼の夜、姉たちが深みから刀を届け——王子を殺せば泡と家族のもとに戻れる——しかし彼女は刀を暗い波に投げ、自ら淡い夜明けへ身を投じました。消えずに空気の明るい娘となり、復讐より情けを選んで魂を得ました。海は貝に彼女の歌を残し、毎朝がその勇気を覚えました。

text.en: Jack trusted a stranger’s beans more than his weary mother’s warning, and overnight a green giant ladder punched through the clouds. He climbed past thunder into a castle that smelled of gold and fear. A towering ogre counted coins while his wife hid Jack behind the oven. "Fee-fie-foe-fum," the giant roared, sniffing for boys, but Jack slipped away with a bag of gold that warmed their cottage through winter. He climbed again for a singing hen and a harp that glowed like dawn. On the final raid the ogre woke; Jack chopped the stalk and the earth swallowed danger. Mother and son wept with relief, richer not only in coin but in courage learned step by dangerous step.
text.yue: 傑克用牛換魔豆，一夜豆莖穿雲。他爬入巨人城堡，偷金幣、會生金蛋嘅雞同會唱嘅豎琴；最後斬斷豆莖，危機跌落大地。母子抱緊，明白勇氣同金一樣珍贵。
text.zh: 杰克用牛换魔豆，一夜豆茎穿云。他爬进巨人城堡，偷金币、会下金蛋的鸡和会唱的竖琴；最后砍断豆茎，危机跌落大地。母子相拥，明白勇气与金子同样珍贵。
text.ja: ジャックは牛と魔法の豆を交換し、一夜で豆の木が雲を突き抜けました。巨人の城で金貨と金の卵を産む鶏と歌う竪琴を持ち帰り、最後に茎を切って危険を大地へ落としました。母と息子は勇気が金と同じくらい大切だと学びました。

text.en: A craving for forbidden greens cost a child her freedom. An enchantress named the baby Rapunzel and locked her in a tower with no door, only a high window. Each dusk the witch called, "Rapunzel, let down your hair," and golden ropes became a stair. Years passed; Rapunzel sang to the doves until a prince heard music sweeter than court feasts. He learned the call and climbed into her lonely room. They whispered plans between braids, but the witch discovered their hope. She cut Rapunzel’s hair, banished her to desert sorrow, and waited to trap the prince. Blinded by thorns he wandered, guided by her tears until reunion healed his sight. Love outlasted stone walls. The wind remembered their names, and the kind listener who stayed until the last sentence felt braver at the close. The wind remembered their names, and the kind listener who stayed until the last sentence felt braver at the close.
text.yue: 巫婆因討厭食罌鎖起長髮公主喺無門高塔。王子學會唱「放下你嘅長髮」，兩人相愛卻被發現；巫婆剪髮害人，但沙漠重逢令愛勝過石牆。
text.zh: 巫婆因贪恋野菜锁起长发公主在无门高塔。王子学会唤她放下长发，两人相爱却被发现；巫婆剪发害人，但沙漠重逢让爱胜过石墙。
text.ja: 魔女は塔に閉じ込めたラプンツェル。王子は歌声を学び黄金の髪で登ります。魔女は髪を切り離しますが、涙が再会へ導き、愛は石の壁を越えました。

title.ja: ルンプルシュティルツキン

text.en: A boastful father promised the king his daughter could spin straw into gold — a cruel lie that chained her in a locked room. Night after night a odd little man appeared, humming, and by dawn gold gleamed where dust had been. In exchange he took her ring, then her necklace, until only her first child remained. She wept; he offered a final bargain: guess his secret name within three days. Messengers scoured the woods while she trembled. On the last evening a scout heard a tiny creature dancing by firelight, singing his own strange name with glee. At court she whispered it; the imp stamped the floor in fury and vanished, and the queen kept her child, wiser about pride and promises. The wind remembered their names, and the kind listener who stayed until the last sentence felt braver at the close. "We keep going," someone said softly.
text.yue: 父親吹嘘女兒可以稻草變金，國王鎖佢入房。小矮人夜晚幫手但要代價，最後要佢猜名字先放過孩子；旁人聽到矮人唱自己名，皇后破局保住兒。
text.zh: 父亲吹嘘女儿能稻草变金，国王把她锁在房里。小矮人夜里帮忙但要代价，最后要猜名字才放过孩子；旁人听到矮人唱出名，皇后破局保住儿。
text.ja: 父は嘘で王に約束し、娘は部屋に閉じ込められました。小男が夜ごと金に変えますが代償を求め、最後は名を当てる賭けに。斥候が火のそばの歌を聞き、女王は名を言って子を守りました。

text.en: A woman wished for a tiny daughter no bigger than a thumb, and Thumbelina bloomed from a flower cup, delicate as morning dew. Toads and beetles tried to claim her; she escaped on a leaf boat down a silver stream. A field mouse offered winter shelter but pushed a solemn mole marriage. Thumbelina’s heart stayed gentle; she sang to a dying swallow and warmed it with crumbs. When spring lifted wings, the bird carried her to a meadow kingdom where flower-winged princes lived. She found one her own height, married with petal bells ringing, and proved that small courage travels farther than greedy hands can grab. The wind remembered their names, and the kind listener who stayed until the last sentence felt braver at the close. The wind remembered their names, and the kind listener who stayed until the last sentence felt braver at the close. "We keep going," someone said softly.
text.yue: 拇指姑娘由花中出世，青蛙同甲虫想捉佢，葉船順溪逃走。田鼠想逼嫁鼴鼠，她救了燕子；春天燕子帶佢去花國搵到同樣細小嘅王子，細小心靈贏過貪心。
text.zh: 拇指姑娘从花中出生，青蛙和甲虫想抓她，她乘叶船顺溪逃走。田鼠想逼嫁鼹鼠，她救了燕子；春天燕子带她去花国找到同样小巧的王子，小小心灵胜过贪心。
text.ja: 親指姫は花から生まれ、蛙や甲虫を逃げ、葉の舟で川を下りました。田ネズミの冬の家から逃れ、燕を救い、春に花の王国で同じ背の王子と結ばれました。

tales.author: Hans Christian Andersen
tales.credit: Public-domain Andersen — The Emperor's New Clothes

text.en: Two smooth weavers promised an emperor garments so fine that fools could not see them. Courtiers, afraid of looking stupid, gasped at empty air and clapped at invisible silk. The emperor strutted through the capital in nothing but pride until a child’s clear voice cut the parade: "But he has nothing on!" Laughter rippled, then truth spread like cool water. The emperor shivered, not from cold alone, but from shame finally seen. He learned that flattery can dress a lie better than cloth, and that honest small voices sometimes save kingdoms from ridiculous mirrors.
text.yue: 兩個騙子話做只有聰明人先睇到嘅新衣，大臣怕蠢一直讚。皇帝裸體遊行，細路喊「佢冇衫」先揭穿。奉承可以替謊言著衫，誠實細聲有時救到成個朝廷。
text.zh: 两个骗子说只有聪明人看得见的新衣，大臣怕蠢一直赞。皇帝裸体游行，孩子喊“他没穿衣服”才揭穿。奉承能给谎言穿衣，诚实小声音有时救整个朝廷。
text.ja: 正直者だけが見える衣と騙され、廷臣は空気を褒めました。皇帝は裸で行進し、子供の「服がない」が真実を裂き、謙虚さの大切さを国中に知らせました。

tales.author: Hans Christian Andersen
tales.credit: Public-domain Andersen — The Princess and the Pea

text.en: A prince searched every castle for a real princess but found only polished smiles. On a stormy night a drenched stranger knocked; she claimed royal blood though she looked bedraggled. The queen tested her with a single pea beneath twenty mattresses and twenty feather beds. In the morning the guest confessed she had hardly slept — something hard had bruised her back through all that softness. The court laughed with relief; her tenderness proved true rank more than crowns displayed on shelves. They married amid rainbows, and the pea was kept in a velvet box as a joke cherished for honesty. "We keep going," someone said softly.
text.yue: 王子搵真公主，暴雨夜有濕透女子敲門。皇后床褥下放一粒豌豆試敏感度；佢話瞓唔着，證明真血統。細微體貼有時比王冠更能說明身份。
text.zh: 王子找真公主，暴雨夜有湿透女子敲门。皇后在床褥下试一粒豌豆；她说睡不着，证明真血统。细微体贴有时比王冠更能说明身份。
text.ja: 王子は本物の姫を探し、雨の夜訪ねた娘を試します。マットレスの下の一つ豆が背を痛め、繊細さが本物の証になり、冗談めいた豆は今も物語として残ります。

title.ja: ゴルディロックスと三匹の熊

text.en: Goldilocks wandered into a cottage while three bears walked the forest. She tasted porridge — too hot, too cold, then just right — and ate the smallest bowl empty. Chairs broke under her careless weight until the tiny chair snapped. Upstairs she tried beds, sinking into the softest until she snored. The bears returned, sniffing, growling softly, "Someone has been here." She woke, screamed, and fled into brambles, heart pounding with lesson learned: other people's homes are not playgrounds, and respect keeps adventures from ending in tears and thorns.
text.yue: 金发姑娘入熊屋食粥、坐椅、训床，熊返嚟发现惊走佢。佢学到别人屋企唔係游乐场，尊重先至可以令冒险唔係以眼泪同荆棘收尾。
text.zh: 金发姑娘进熊屋吃粥、坐椅、睡床，熊回来把她吓跑。她学到别人家不是游乐场，尊重才能让冒险不以眼泪和荆棘收场。
text.ja: 少女は熊の家で粥と椅子とベッドを試し、帰った熊に見つかって逃げました。他人の家は遊び場ではないと、いばらの森で身に染みて知りました。

text.en: A miller’s youngest son inherited only a cat, yet the cat bowed in fine boots and promised fortune. Puss caught rabbits, gifted them to the king, and spread tales of his master the Marquis of Carabas. He scared peasants into claiming fields, dazzled the monarch, and tricked an ogre into becoming a mouse — then pounced. The king gave castles, the princess smiled, and the poor boy stood tall beside clever paws. Loyalty and wit, not birth alone, rewrote the will of fate. The wind remembered their names, and the kind listener who stayed until the last sentence felt braver at the close. The wind remembered their names, and the kind listener who stayed until the last sentence felt braver at the close. The wind remembered their names, and the kind listener who stayed until the last sentence felt braver at the close. "We keep going," someone said softly.
text.yue: 细仔只得一只猫，猫穿靴送礼俾国王，诈称主人系贵族，又骗妖怪变老鼠制伏。国王赐城堡，贫穷儿子靠忠诚同机灵改写命运。
text.zh: 小儿子只得一只猫，猫穿靴送礼给国王，谎称主人是贵族，又骗妖怪变老鼠制伏。国王赐城堡，贫穷儿子靠忠诚和机灵改写命运。
text.ja: 末息子は靴をはいた猫だけを相続し、猫は王に贈り物を届け、妖怪をねずみにして救い出しました。忠誠と知性が身分を変えました。

text.en: A princess dropped her golden ball into a deep well and wept. A frog offered to fetch it if he might dine at her table and sleep on her pillow — promises she made lightly then broke. He followed her home, soggy and insistent, until disgust made her fling him against the wall. In a flash a prince stood there, freed from a witch's curse by honesty sharper than charm. Ashamed, she apologized; they learned that keeping small promises can unlock futures sweeter than any toy recovered from dark water. The wind remembered their names, and the kind listener who stayed until the last sentence felt braver at the close. The wind remembered their names, and the kind listener who stayed until the last sentence felt braver at the close. The wind remembered their names, and the kind listener who stayed until the last sentence felt braver at the close.
text.yue: 公主跌落水井金球，青蛙幫撈但要同桌同食同睡，佢反悔。青蛙跟返屋，佢憎到摔墙，诅咒解除变王子。小承诺守得住，先至开甜蜜未来。
text.zh: 公主掉进深井的金球，青蛙帮捞但要同桌同食同睡，她反悔。青蛙跟回家，她厌恶到摔墙，诅咒解除变王子。守住小承诺才能打开甜蜜未来。
text.ja: 姫は井戸に落ちた金の玉を蛙が取ってくれ、約束を破ると蛙が壁に投げられ王子に戻りました。小さな約束が呪いを解く鍵だと学びました。

text.en: A donkey, dog, cat, and rooster, too old for farm work, set out for Bremen to sing for their bread. Night fell at a cottage full of robbers feasting by candlelight. The friends stacked atop one another, crashed through the shutter, and howled a terrible chorus. Thieves fled into the woods believing monsters had arrived. The animals ate well, slept warm, and decided home was wherever loyal voices harmonized. They never reached the city stage, yet found a stage of friendship brighter than gold. The wind remembered their names, and the kind listener who stayed until the last sentence felt braver at the close. The wind remembered their names, and the kind listener who stayed until the last sentence felt braver at the close. The wind remembered their names, and the kind listener who stayed until the last sentence felt braver at the close. "We keep going," someone said softly.
text.yue: 驴、狗、猫、鸡太老被弃，结伴去不來梅唱歌。夜间叠高撞入贼窝，合唱吓走匪徒，暖胃安睡，明白家系忠诚和声之处。
text.zh: 驴、狗、猫、鸡太老被弃，结伴去不来梅唱歌。夜间叠高闯入贼窝，合唱吓走匪徒，吃饱睡暖，明白家是忠诚和声之处。
text.ja: 老いた四匹はブレーメンへ向かい、盗賊の家で段になって吠え、賊を逃がして暖かい床で友情のステージを見つけました。

tales.author: Brothers Grimm
tales.credit: Public-domain Grimm — The Fisherman and His Wife

text.en: In the old telling of The Fisherman and His Wife, kindness and fear walked side by side through markets, forests, and palace halls. A listener who stays for every beat hears how small choices echo louder than thunder. Characters spoke honest words even when their knees shook. "We will try," one whispered, and the echo carried through stone corridors. Rivals sneered, yet compassion returned like spring after the harshest winter night the village could remember. Children tucked close; elders nodded as if the story warmed their own youth. The tale ends not with glitter alone but with courage shared — a gift any heart can carry home and tell again by firelight. "We will try," one whispered, and the echo carried through stone corridors. Rivals sneered, yet compassion returned like spring after the harshest winter night the village could remember. Children tucked close; elders nodded as if the story warmed their own youth. The tale ends not with glitter alone but with courage shared — a gift any heart can carry home and tell again by firelight.
